annotationRationale: Equally likely assignments turn the probability ratio into a counting ratio. Combinations count the ball selections, and the multiplication principle combines the choices of bins and balls.
sourceMethod: Follows the first official solution comparing 3-and-5 versus 4-and-4 splits of eight balls. Introduces a common factor K and fixes the comparison bins to make cancellation and counting multiplicities explicit.

review.mathCheck: All labeled assignments have probability 5^(-20). For fixed special bins the numerator count is 20!/[3!5!(4!)³], while the denominator count is 20!/(4!)⁵. There are 20 choices of special bins, giving p/q=20(4!)²/(3!5!)=16, choice E.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded expansion of the first MAA Q21 solution, page 10. The common factor K makes cancellation explicit, while fixed bin labels resolve the source's compressed counting argument.
review.annotationCheck: Independent tosses justify equiprobable assignments. Unique special bins and fixed labels prevent overcounting in both events. All combination counts and the stated key are correct; the explanation needs no multinomial prerequisite.
